# v4 Phase 4.3 — Daily, Made Hard: Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Rebuild `DAILY_CALENDAR` around ~40 longer, harder scrubber / drag-order / tap-line puzzles (no mcq, no swipe-binary), generated by a subagent through the existing zero-API offline content tooling and checked by an independent review subagent, with the new length bar enforced by a failing build rather than a comment.

**Architecture:** No new interaction component. `ScrubberSchema`'s checkpoint ceiling moves from 4 to 8 (nothing in `TraceRunner`/`useTraceSession` hardcodes a count — both are driven entirely by `puzzle.checkpoints.length`), and the offline authoring harness (`authorScrubberPuzzles.ts`) gets the matching cap so a subagent can produce valid content without any Anthropic API call. `DragOrderSchema`/`TapLineSchema` already have no upper size bound, so their "harder" batch is pure content, gated by a new build-enforced length check on `DAILY_CALENDAR` specifically (not the whole pool). Content is produced by one subagent (generation) and checked by a second, independent subagent (review) before the calendar is rebuilt from the result.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript, Zod, Vitest, the existing `src/content/tools/` offline authoring pipeline (`authorScrubberPuzzles.ts`, `traceGen/`), Node child-process execution (for hand-verifying drag-order/tap-line ground truth), Claude Code subagents (Agent tool) — no Anthropic API key touched anywhere in this plan.

**Spec:** `docs/v4-build-plan.md`, Phase 4.3 (amended 2026-08-28) — see that section for the full DoD checklist this plan implements against.

## Global Constraints

- **No mcq or swipe-binary in `DAILY_CALENDAR`**, ever — firm, re-confirmed rule.
- **Difficulty floor ≥1600** for every Daily entry — unchanged by this batch.
- **Calendar target ~40 entries**, rebuilt from scratch — legal only because `DAILY_EPOCH` is still the `2026-01-01` placeholder (`dailyCalendar.ts`'s own pre-launch note). The day the real epoch is frozen, this becomes forbidden.
- **No Anthropic API calls anywhere in this batch.** Scrubber content goes through the existing offline harness; drag-order/tap-line are hand-authored and self-verified by actually executing the snippet.
- **Drop-don't-patch**: any puzzle that fails review is discarded and regenerated from scratch, never edited to "fix" it — same convention `GENERATING_PUZZLES.md` already documents for the API pipeline.
- `generateScrubberPuzzles.ts`'s `PlacementSchema` (its own separate `.max(4)`, used only by the API-calling pipeline this batch never touches) is deliberately **left unchanged** — out of scope, not an oversight.
- `pnpm validate` (typecheck + lint + test + validate:content + build) green after every task.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement**

In `src/content/tools/authorScrubberPuzzles.ts`:

- Line 50 (doc comment) and its surrounding paragraph — update "3–4 checkpoints" to "6–8 checkpoints" so the file's own documentation doesn't drift from what it enforces.
- Line 116:
  ```ts
  checkpoints: z.array(AuthorCheckpointSchema).min(2).max(8).optional(),
  ```
- Line 162: add `export` before `function distinctQuestionTypes`.
- Lines 207-210 (`authoringRuleViolations`), export it and update the bound:

  ```ts
  export function authoringRuleViolations(
    checkpoints: readonly CandidateCheckpoint[],
  ): string | null {
    if (checkpoints.length < 6 || checkpoints.length > 8) {
      return `expected 6-8 checkpoints, got ${String(checkpoints.length)}`
    }
    if (distinctQuestionTypes(checkpoints) < 2) {
      return `needs >=2 distinct question types across next-line/var-value/output, got only ${String(new Set(checkpoints.map((c) => c.question)).size)} type(s)`
    }
    return null
  }
  ```

## Task 4: Generation subagent — author the content batch

**Not a code task.** This task's deliverable is puzzle files on disk, produced by dispatching a subagent (Agent tool), not by writing code in this plan.

**Target mix for ~40 calendar entries** (default split — adjust only if Task 6's assembly finds a real shortfall in one type): **16 scrubber, 12 drag-order, 12 tap-line**, every one difficulty ≥1600, spanning the patterns each interaction type is already allowed for (scrubber's existing allowlist in `authorScrubberPuzzles.ts:88-96`; drag-order/tap-line have no such allowlist — any pattern is fine).

- [ ] **Step 1: Dispatch the generation subagent**

Use the Agent tool (`subagent_type: "implementer"` or `general-purpose`) with a prompt covering, verbatim:

1. Read `src/content/GENERATING_PUZZLES.md`, `src/content/CALIBRATION.md`, and this plan's Task 4/5 sections in full before writing anything.
2. For **scrubber** (target: 16 puzzles, 6-8 checkpoints each, ≥1600 difficulty, patterns from `authorScrubberPuzzles.ts`'s `SCRUBBER_PATTERN_ALLOWLIST`): write an intents JSON file, run `pnpm author:scrubber-puzzles --intents=<path> --preview` first to see the real trace and place checkpoints against actual steps (not guessed), then run the write pass (`pnpm author:scrubber-puzzles --intents=<path>`). Snippets should be long/tricky enough to sustain 6-8 genuinely distinct checkpoints — realistically this means two functions or one function with real branching, not a 4-line stub.
3. For **drag-order** (target: 12 puzzles, 8-10 blocks each, ≥1600 difficulty): hand-author puzzle JSON matching `DragOrderSchema` (`src/content/schema.ts:107-112`). **Self-verify the real execution order before writing** — actually run each snippet (`node` for JS, `python3` for Python) and confirm `blocks`/`correct_order` match real output, the same rigor the trace generator gives scrubber automatically. Use the `puzzleAuthoringShared.ts` id-counter convention (`createIdCounters`) so ids don't collide with existing content.
4. For **tap-line** (target: 12 puzzles, snippet ≥15 lines, a genuinely subtle bug, ≥1600 difficulty): hand-author puzzle JSON matching `TapLineSchema` (`src/content/schema.ts:73-76`). Self-verify `correct_line` by actually tracing the snippet's logic, not just asserting it.
5. After every puzzle: run `pnpm validate:content` — a puzzle that fails schema validation is dropped and rewritten, never patched to force a pass.
6. Report back: the full list of new puzzle ids written, grouped by interaction type, with each one's difficulty rating and (for scrubber) checkpoint count / (for drag-order) block count / (for tap-line) snippet line count, so Task 5's reviewer doesn't have to re-derive this from scratch.

- [ ] **Step 2: Verify the batch is schema-valid and complete**

Run: `pnpm validate:content && pnpm content:stats`
Expected: exit 0, and `content:stats`'s interaction/difficulty breakdown shows the new puzzles present at the target counts (or close — see the adjustment note above).

## Task 5: Review subagent — independent correctness + calibration pass

**Not a code task.** Deliverable is a pass/fail verdict per puzzle from Task 4, with discards regenerated by re-running Task 4 for just the failed ids — not patched.

- [ ] **Step 1: Dispatch the review subagent (fresh context — must not be the same subagent instance that generated the batch)**

Prompt covering, verbatim:

1. You are reviewing a content batch you did not write. Read `src/content/GENERATING_PUZZLES.md`'s "The self-review pass doesn't replace you" section and `CALIBRATION.md`'s S/T/D/C rubric before reviewing anything.
2. For every puzzle id reported by Task 4: **blind re-estimate its difficulty** against `CALIBRATION.md` before looking at the stored `difficulty_rating`, then compare — flag any puzzle whose stored rating is more than ±200 off your blind estimate.
3. Confirm the claimed defect/order/trace is real: for scrubber, re-derive at least 2 of the checkpoints by hand against the snippet; for drag-order, confirm `correct_order` actually matches real execution order (re-run the snippet yourself, don't trust the generation subagent's self-report); for tap-line, confirm `correct_line` is the actual root cause, not a symptom.
4. Judge pacing: does this puzzle plausibly take a competent player 1-2 minutes, not 20 seconds and not 5 minutes? Flag anything that reads as padded-but-not-actually-harder (e.g. checkpoints that ask the same thing twice in different words).
5. Run `pnpm validate:content` and `pnpm content:stats` yourself — don't trust Task 4's report of these.
6. Produce a verdict per puzzle id: **PASS** or **DISCARD (reason)**. Any `DISCARD` puzzle gets deleted (its file removed) — it will be regenerated in a follow-up Task 4 dispatch for just the gap, never patched in place.

- [ ] **Step 2: Act on the verdict**

For every `DISCARD`, delete that puzzle's file and re-dispatch a scoped Task 4 subagent for just the shortfall (same target mix, reduced count). Repeat Task 4 → Task 5 until every remaining candidate is a clean PASS and the pool has enough puzzles per type to hit ~40 total (16/12/12 or the adjusted split).

## Task 7: Give Daily a scrubber-capable render path (added 2026-08-29 — critical finding from Task 6's review)

Task 6's independent review found, and the controller independently confirmed by reading both files directly, that `DailyPage.tsx` cannot render a scrubber puzzle: it routes every puzzle through `PuzzleCardShell`, which has an explicit `case 'scrubber': throw` (`src/app/practice/PuzzleCardShell.tsx:443-448`) — a deliberate P0-era guard (`docs/v2-phase2-review.md`) built on the assumption that Practice/Daily/Rush structurally never see a scrubber puzzle. That assumption predates this plan and is now false: `DAILY_CALENDAR` (rebuilt in Task 6) has 16 scrubber entries in it, and Daily's real puzzle-fetch path (`useDailySession.ts` → `getPuzzleBody`, `src/content/index.ts`) has no interaction-type filter that would stop one from reaching the renderer. This is a gap in the _original_ `docs/v4-build-plan.md` Phase 4.3 design, not something Tasks 1-6 introduced — nothing in that plan or this one ever touched `PuzzleCardShell`/`DailyPage` before now.

**Design (approved by direct user decision, 2026-08-29):** reuse `TraceRunnerPuzzle` (`src/app/trace/TraceRunner.tsx`), which is already exported as a self-contained, puzzle-in/callback-out component (`TraceRunnerPuzzleProps`: `puzzle`, `checkpointResults`, `isComplete`, `solved`, `ratingDelta`, `onCheckpointAnswered`, `onContinue`, `timed?`) — it is NOT coupled to `useTraceSession`; that coupling lives only in the outer `TraceRunner` container, which this task does not touch. Scrubber puzzles today render only via `/trace`; Practice/Rush/Boss/Puzzle/Challenge all correctly continue excluding them for their own unrelated reasons (Rush's interaction exclusion, Boss's binary-strike/partial-credit mismatch) — this fix is Daily-only.

**Build:**

1. **`src/app/daily/useDailySession.ts`**: add scrubber-specific session state — an accumulated `checkpointResults: readonly CheckpointResult[]` (from `src/engine/scrubber.ts`'s `CheckpointResult` type), derived `isComplete` (`checkpointResults.length >= puzzle.checkpoints.length`) and `solved` (via the existing `scoreScrubberAttempt`, same as Trace mode uses). Add an `onCheckpointAnswered: (result: CheckpointResult) => void` callback that appends to `checkpointResults` and, once complete, runs the same rating/streak/persistence/telemetry path `handleAnswered` already runs for non-scrubber puzzles — refactor the shared "commit an attempt" logic into one helper both paths call rather than duplicating it. Only applies when `puzzle.interaction === 'scrubber'`; the existing `handleAnswered`/`CommitPayload` path is unchanged for every other interaction type.
2. **`src/app/daily/DailyPage.tsx`**: branch on `session.puzzle.interaction === 'scrubber'` — render `<TraceRunnerPuzzle puzzle={session.puzzle} checkpointResults={...} isComplete={...} solved={...} ratingDelta={session.ratingDelta} onCheckpointAnswered={session.onCheckpointAnswered} onContinue={session.handleRetry} timed={false} />` instead of `<PuzzleCardShell .../>`. `timed={false}` matches Daily's existing no-per-puzzle-timer feel (same value `/trace` itself uses, todo item 14's "no timer on regular trace mode" precedent).
3. **Tests**: add real coverage for a scrubber-day `DailyPage`/`useDailySession` render — the exact gap Task 6's review found (`DailyPage.test.tsx`'s fixture pool is all-mcq; `App.test.tsx`'s real-content Daily test happens to land on a non-scrubber date). Cover: checkpoint answers accumulate correctly, completion triggers the same rating/streak/persistence path as a non-scrubber Daily puzzle, and a scrubber puzzle no longer throws.

**DoD:**

- [ ] A scrubber puzzle placed in `DAILY_CALENDAR` renders via `TraceRunnerPuzzle`, not `PuzzleCardShell`, and does not throw
- [ ] Completing a scrubber Daily puzzle produces the same rating/streak/`dailyCompletion`/telemetry effects a non-scrubber Daily puzzle does (verified by test, not just code inspection)
- [ ] `PuzzleCardShell.tsx`'s `case 'scrubber': throw` is untouched — Practice/Rush/Boss/Puzzle/Challenge still correctly exclude scrubber
- [ ] `TraceRunner.tsx`, `useTraceSession.ts` untouched — zero regression risk to `/trace`
- [ ] New test coverage exercises an actual scrubber-day render (not an all-mcq fixture), catching the exact gap this task exists to close
- [ ] `pnpm validate` green
